tasks.spec:
You are a Python engineer. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge (detached at HEAD). Edit files here directly. NEVER git commit, never touch /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge itself, never run `uv`, never call a billed model or the network. FIRST run: [ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv ; run tests as `PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 0 <files>` (never pass --cov); ruff as `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check <files>` and `.venv/bin/python -m ruff format <files>` (line length 120, double quotes, Python 3.12, PyYAML and pydantic only, no new dependencies).

BACKGROUND. The game's story data now loads from a declarative source tree, `data/stories/continuity-initiative/source/` (story.yaml, catalog.yaml, scenes/<id>.yaml and scenes/<id>.match.yaml), which `storygame.story_source.compile_source_tree` compiles to the same `StoryPackage` the nine legacy files produced. The frozen legacy files are at `tests/fixtures/parity/continuity-initiative/legacy/`; `storygame.story_package.loader.load_legacy_story_package(Path(...))` loads them, and `load_story_package(Path("data/stories/continuity-initiative"))` loads the compiled default. The format is fixed by `.plans/story-data-schema-contract.md` (read sections 2, 4.3, 4.9, 5 and 9 first). The converter (`storygame/story_source/convert*.py`, entry `convert_package` and `write_source_tree`) wrote the committed source tree from the legacy package and the parity checker (`parity.py`, gate test `tests/story_source/test_parity_default.py`, which you must not edit) compares the two packages.

THE DEFECT, measured. The order of records INSIDE one scene is part of behaviour, and the compiled package gets it wrong. Example: `bench.core.establish_prior_beats` fires storylets in `package.storylets` order, and an earlier firing can block a later one. For scene 1B the legacy order is SL-1B-D, A, E, F, G, H, B, C but the compiled order is D, A, E, B, C, F, G, H, so `python -m bench prompt --scene 1B --beat 1B.4 --text` differs between the compiled package and the legacy one by the line "- The thermos carries a county emergency-water label." The parity gate did not notice because `_COLLECTION_FIELDS` in `parity.py` makes ANY reorder of `storylets`, `knowledge`, `deliveries`, `events`, `scenes`, `facts` and `realizations` count as `collection_order`, which is reviewed automatically. The contract is stricter: section 9 says `collection_order` applies only "when a keyed record moves ONLY ACROSS SCENES; its relative order among same-scene records is unchanged". Moving a record from one scene's block to another's position is still allowed; reordering records of the same scene is not.
The independent check script (never edit it, it lives in the main repo at /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/story-data/check_order_parity.py) lists every within-scene difference and every differing prompt. Run it first: `PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src .venv/bin/python /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/scripts/ringer/story-data/check_order_parity.py`. On HEAD it reports differences for storylets in 1A, 1B and 2C; deliveries in 1B, 2A, 2B, 2C, 3B and 3C; knowledge claims in 1C, 2A, 2B, 2C and 3C; and the 1B.4 prompt. `storylet_routes.storylets` already agrees; the legacy package keeps TWO different orders, one for the routes (storylet-routes.yaml) and one for the storylets (storylets.md), while the compiler builds both from one `reveals` list, so the reveals order must stay the route order and the storylet order needs its own record.

YOUR JOB, in this order.
1. Make the parity tool follow the contract. In `parity.py`, a reorder of same-scene records of any keyed collection (`storylets`, `storylet_routes.storylets`, `knowledge.knowledge`, `deliveries`, `pacing.events`, and every other list that `_COLLECTION_FIELDS` covers except `world.facts` which keeps its existing, separate proof) must NOT be `collection_order`: classify it as `representation`, which is reviewable only with a reason, so the gate fails until the compiled order matches. Movement of a record relative to records of OTHER scenes stays `collection_order` (auto). Do not add review entries for any of this. Write `tests/story_source/test_parity_within_scene_order.py` with small synthetic package dumps in the style of `test_parity_core.py`: a pure cross-scene move passes as `collection_order`; a same-scene swap is unreviewed and the summary fails; an entry with the right class, path and digests still reviews it. Update existing tests that pinned the old lenient behaviour (only `test_parity_core.py` and `test_f23_parity_classes.py`, only where they assert that a same-scene reorder is `collection_order`); say which you changed in NOTES_r7.txt. Then run `tests/story_source/test_parity_default.py` and confirm it now FAILS on the real story with differences exactly in the scenes listed above, before any fix; put the failing paths in NOTES_r7.txt.
2. Add an optional per-scene key `order` to the scene file, so the source can say the order of same-scene records where it differs from the natural one. Shape: a mapping with optional keys `storylets`, `deliveries`, `knowledge` and `pacing_events`, each a list of ids of that scene's records of that kind (storylet ids; delivery fact ids; claim ids including bridge, entry and route-effect claims; pacing event ids). Compiler rule: build every collection in the natural order exactly as today, then, per scene, place that scene's records of that kind in the listed order, ids not listed keeping their natural order after the listed ones; the scene's block keeps its position among the other scenes' blocks. The `order` key goes LAST in the scene file's top-level key order (after `ending`), the layer 1 shape check (`l1_scene.py`) accepts it with those four optional list-of-string keys and rejects anything else, and a new layer 2 check module `l2_order.py` (the registry discovers any `l2_*.py`, see how `l2_story.py` registers) reports a diagnostic `L2.order_id` for an id that is not a record of that kind in that scene, a duplicate id, and `L2.order_noop` is NOT needed. Write `tests/story_source/test_scene_order_key.py`: the order key reorders as specified; absent key changes nothing; unknown id, duplicate id and a wrong-shaped value are rejected with the diagnostic codes; a mini fixture under `tests/fixtures/story_source/` may be copied by the patch helper in `tests/story_source/helpers.py` (read how other tests do it, never edit helpers or existing fixtures). Add the key to the contract: the key table in section 2 (`scenes/<id>.yaml` row), a short new subsection after 4.15 describing the shape, the rule and the diagnostics, and the `collection_order` row in section 9 stated exactly as above.
3. Make the converter write it. `convert_order.py` (new) receives the legacy package and, per scene and per kind, returns the legacy within-scene id order; the converter (`convert.py` / `convert_scene.py`) writes the `order` key into a scene file ONLY for kinds whose legacy within-scene order differs from the natural order the compiler would produce, so a scene with no difference gets no `order` key. Regenerate the committed scene files with the converter: write a fresh conversion into a temp directory (look at how `write_source_tree` and `tests/story_source/test_convert_tree.py` do it), diff it against `data/stories/continuity-initiative/source/`; if the ONLY differences are the new `order` blocks, copy the changed scene files over the committed ones; if anything else differs (the committed tree was edited by hand after conversion), do NOT overwrite: apply only the `order` blocks to the committed scene files by hand, keeping their key order and style, and write what else differed in NOTES_r7.txt. Never change any other value in the source tree.
4. Prove it. Run `tests/story_source/test_parity_default.py` (must pass again with zero unreviewed differences and only the one existing `world.facts` review) and the independent check script (must exit 0: no order differences, all prompts identical). If a prompt still differs after the order matches, the cause is something else: stop, write the exact differing lines and your diagnosis in NOTES_r7.txt, and leave the check failing.

Do not edit the gate test `test_parity_default.py`, the independent check script, `bench/`, the loader, the engine, legacy story data, the world-facts review file, tests/shard_durations.json or any file not in your ownership list. Do not add review entries to hide an order difference. Do not make the compiler sort by id or by any rule: the order must come from the source tree. If something needs a contract change beyond section 2, 4.16 and 9 as described, write it in NOTES_r7.txt and leave the failure visible.

TESTS: all of tests/story_source must pass at the end; do not add tests beyond the two new files named above.
